scenes.line1: Why does branching matter in Git?
scenes.say: Ever wondered why branching is at the heart of Git? Let’s break down why it’s the key to smooth teamwork.

scenes.label: Commit
scenes.sub: A commit snapshots your project at a moment.
scenes.say: A commit is your code’s snapshot. It records changes and keeps your history safe.
Branches let you work in parallel. HEAD shows where you are. Remote tracking helps you sync with others.
Merging preserves all history and adds a merge commit. Rebasing rewrites history for a cleaner timeline.

scenes.title: Resolving Conflicts
scenes.say: When branches overlap, conflicts pop up. Git flags the files, and you fix them before finishing the merge.

scenes.question: Should you rebase a shared branch?
scenes.right: No, rebasing shared branches rewrites history and can cause confusion or lost commits.
scenes.say: Here’s a common trap: rebasing shared branches can mess up history for your teammates. Avoid it.
